body.text: Run began at 2026-11-15T19:14:47Z (status start_utc). Stage 1 reconstruction runs through 20:14:47Z; no training simulation before that deadline. Task: sequentially grasp 2 or 3 lying charger plugs on the right, turn each using active fingers with a demonstration-like wrist, then release it upright blades-up on the left. Unknown object identity/scale, contacts and wrist rotation will be investigated from the video before criteria are frozen.

Direct video inspection supports fixed blades, not a folding mechanism. White resembles an Apple 18/20W adapter (public ChargerLAB 41×42×27 mm, 59g prior). Black branding is unreadable and its body appears shorter than Samsung EP-TA200 (56.6mm); I will fit relative dimensions rather than claim that identity. SAM3 initial black prompt misses early frames; retrying a less specific prompt. A single manually clicked white corner calibration produced an unbounded focal estimate, so it is not evidence of a calibrated focal.

The automatic white silhouette fit has an incorrect blade-axis permutation at frame 0 despite IoU 0.92. Rejected that orientation. Added manually identified blade/port-end constraints, gravity-aligned resting side and upright-end fits. A single shared support plane exposed black scale inconsistency: initial/final black fits lay about 12 mm above the white-derived table. Testing a 5% larger black body estimated from common support, keeping blade dimensions fixed; no claim of a measured black identity or mass.

body.text: Reconstruction v1 r0004 is output-contract VALID but quality failures are explicit. V2 local MANO losses restore opposed thumb/finger contact on 100% of evaluated contact frames (from 3.4%/32.9%), but full-mesh penetration remains 6.7/11.23mm and self-intersections 33.3%, despite sparse-probe score improving to 2.8mm. Next refinement uses all 778 vertices for penetration, a stronger distal separation prior, and lower optimizer steps. Also removing silhouette-driven motion before visible pickup and after placement; static support observations take precedence over drifting masks.

body.text: V3 reference r0007 passes all ten validation checks, while depth remains conditional on geometry. The minimum-turn object-relative rotations are78.9deg white (3.5–4.5s; axis[.368,.905,.214]) and69.2deg black (10.4–11.1s; axis[-.309,.948,.075]); wrist turns20.5/31.1deg. A static-area camera-depth sensitivity test gives corrections≤10.7mm (world Z−5.8 to+8.2mm); comparing its full checks before selecting any change. Human phase palm tilt is explicitly measured and is not uniformly palm-down.

Additional reference relation check found a gap beyond the provided ten checks: MANO hand vertices penetrate the table plane by up to32.3mm. The fitter ObjectScene contact list contains only task objects, so dense plug penetration losses did not include table support. Adding an explicit all-vertex tabletop half-space penalty in my local fitter and refitting affected frames. Prior statements that the ten provided checks pass remain true, but do not establish table-safe reconstruction; no training simulation has been built.

The camera-depth variant adds≤10.7mm model-dependent corrections but only changes median IoU .784→.787 white and .760→.765 black, with worse lower-percentile agreement and reintroduced self intersections. Keeping the V3 camera model. Additional tabletop constraint refit reduces worst hand-plane depth32.3mm→0.63mm in affected valid frames; full image/contact checks and comparison now pending. The added relation check is separate from the provided validator.

body.text: Pickup feasibility r0017 passed18/32 fresh starts with zero hardware violations. I viewed both failure montages and a success. Seed622633939 misses the black body during descent/closure around2.1–3.5s, then rises empty; seed1549602001 appears to lift the white but is rejected by the strict opposed/style criteria, requiring contact/pose diagnosis. The nominal end-pinch turning search immediately loses thumb contact when IK substitutes measured pad positions for compressed motor targets, and its final IK error reaches34mm. I will preserve preload during contact trajectory construction and search hand-relative object motion, rather than treating contact surface points as unconstrained position commands. Scripted controllers remain feasibility-only.

body.text: GPU feasibility search budget: up to30min of4096-world offline CEM, then CPU physical replay and fresh handoff gates; no search controller will be called learned. The kinematic end-pinch paths fail because contact preload and finger-body interference matter. Search now optimizes two smooth joint-target knots plus wrist motion per0.8s block, rewarding full object orientation, active relative rotation and opposed retention while penalizing passive rotation, drop and hardware violations. Static scene identical CPU/GPU. State parity275 own contact states has1.1% contact-set mismatch and no overflow at160/480 buffers; qacc warnings on settled objects require outcome parity before GPU PPO. Bench4096 worlds25,093 transitions/s, no overflow at96/600. PPO method budget after teacher repair:50M transitions initial and up to200M if criterion curves keep improving, BC initialization plus free-standing deployable PPO actor; history4–6steps, all motion commands from network.

Nominal CPU turn proof candidate: offline CEM two-block commands alone drift to36deg tilt; IK orientation feedback gain.05 from1.6s preserves an opposed grip with74.9deg relative rotation,8.9deg passive,12.6deg final blade tilt,18.5deg goal-relative orientation error, max joint excess3.22mm-equivalent rad audit below allowance, no hardware violation. This is one nominal state, not chain feasibility yet. Multiobject suite support scope: passive plugs remain on table; support=environment cannot automatically require all scene objects airborne, so turn suite adds explicit environment_contact_s<=.05 for the manipulated object through independent primitive scoring and an any-object standard predicate. No passive contacts are deleted or relabelled.
